customer_james: Having intermittent 500s + big latency spikes since this morning. Request ids: rq_20260317_abc123, rq_20260317_def456. Seems to correlate with model rotation to canary. Can you repro?

lina_support: Sorry about that — can you share a curl repro and the exact model id you saw? If you can't paste logs, we can request a debug bundle.

customer_james: Here's the curl I used (sanitized):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-xxx\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-2b-canary","input":"Summarize the doc"}'
```
Sometimes it returns 200 but with ~40s latency, sometimes 502.

aditya: Can you add a X-Request-ID header or include ?request_id param so we have an exact trace id? Also which region (eu-west-1/us-west-2)?

customer_james: Adding header now: X-Request-ID: rq_20260317_abc123. Region: eu-west-1. I can reproduce with that curl ~30% of attempts.

tina_sre: We saw related warnings in the canary pool around 11:12 UTC — inflight queue grew then. @aditya let's check canary routing & fallback policy. Do we have flow logs for rq_20260317_abc123?

eng_ops: Quick checklist to collect repro artifacts:
- exact X-Request-ID header
- raw response body + status code
- curl -v output (headers + timing)
- client timestamp and rate of requests
- whether you pinned a specific model version or relied on default routing
If the customer can run our debug bundle helper that's the fastest path.

lina_support: Share steps for the debug bundle please — customer has limited infra access.

eng_ops: Ask them to POST to our debug endpoint:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug/bundle \n -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-collector\" \n -H \"X-Request-ID: rq_20260317_abc123\" \n -d '{"include_logs":true,"max_minutes":60}'
```
Response will be a signed S3 URL. If they can't run it we can pull traces internally once we have X-Request-ID.

aditya: Also note: if you pin to model 'redwood-2b-stable' the traffic shouldn't hit canary. Can you confirm whether your app sets a model pin or relies on default 'redwood-2b'?

customer_james: We didn't explicitly pin; our payload uses "model":"redwood-2b" (no suffix), so it may have been routed to canary automatically.

tina_sre: That explains it. Canary is currently configured with prefer-canary:true for a portion of traffic. Fallback should route to stable on error but we've got a bug where 502s from canary skip fallback for batched requests. Marking this P0.

lina_support: For a quick mitigation, two options:
1) Pin to stable by sending "model":"redwood-2b-stable" in the payload
2) Temporarily set header X-Allow-Canary:false
Which would you prefer?

customer_james: I'll pin to stable for now. Can you confirm how to pin in code? Example please.

aditya: Example payload to pin: 
```json
{"model":"redwood-2b-stable","input":"..."}
```
Or set header: X-Model-Pin: redwood-2b-stable
Also we recommend disabling streaming while we investigate if you're using it.

customer_james: Pinned and testing... initial run: 200 in ~350ms. Running more load and will report back. Thanks.

eng_ops: Tracked as INC-2026-1023. @tina will triage the fallback logic, @lina will follow up once we have the debug bundle. Please attach the failing curl output to the ticket.

tina_sre: Assigning to eng-runtime, adding a temporary rule to ensure fallback is synchronous for batched requests. We'll roll a patch to canary tonight and run a smoke test.

support-bot: Reminder: Add reproduction artifacts to INC-2026-1023 in Jira and attach the debug bundle when available. :memo: 

customer_james: Uploaded debug bundle to the signed URL — https://s3.amazonaws.com/example-buckets/rq_20260317_abc123-debug.zip. Let me know when you have anything.
